record.paper_title: Four nucleon systems: a zoom to the open problems in nuclear interaction
record.original_question: What interaction effects are still missing in low-energy neutron plus tritium scattering when a model such as AV18 plus Urbana IX three-nucleon force already reproduces the triton binding energy, yet the coherent scattering lengths remain less clearly consistent with experiment? The question concerns the zero-energy and very-low-energy neutron plus tritium observables, where the zero-energy cross section may fit experimental data while coherent scattering lengths still show small discrepancies.

evidence.quote: However even implementing UIX 3NF for AV18 model, and thus reproducing triton binding energy, small discrepancies remain [11]. If zero energy cross section seems to fit experimental data, agreement for the coherent scattering lengths is less obvious.
Nonlocal interaction model (INOY04) reproduces low n+3H energy data better, this fact is best reflected near the elastic cross section minima around Ecm ∼ 0.4 MeV, see Fig. 2.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the four-nucleon scattering problem for a neutron incident on a triton (3H) at zero and very low energy. The dynamics are governed by a nucleon-nucleon (NN) interaction supplemented by a three-nucleon force (3NF). A representative realistic model is the Argonne v18 (AV18) NN potential combined with the Urbana IX (UIX) three-nucleon force; this combination is tuned to reproduce the experimental triton binding energy (~8.48 MeV).

For the n+3H system at zero energy, two key low-energy observables are:
(i) the zero-energy total cross section σ(0), and
(ii) the spin-dependent coherent scattering lengths a_c (and the singlet a_s and triplet a_t scattering lengths from which a_c is constructed).

Empirically, while AV18+UIX yields a zero-energy cross section in fair agreement with experiment, the coherent (and spin-projected) scattering lengths for n+3H remain in tension with measured values. Nonlocal NN interaction models (such as INOY-type interactions) tend to improve the description of low-energy n+3H data, particularly near the elastic-cross-section minimum at center-of-mass energy E_cm ≈ 0.4 MeV.

Identify and characterize the missing or incompletely modeled interaction ingredients in the nuclear Hamiltonian that are responsible for the residual discrepancies between theoretical predictions (based on AV18+UIX or similar local NN+3NF Hamiltonians that reproduce the triton binding energy) and experimental low-energy n+3H scattering observables — in particular the coherent scattering lengths — while simultaneously preserving agreement with the zero-energy cross section and the triton binding energy. The task is to determine which interaction effects (e.g., specific components of the three-nucleon force, nonlocalities in the NN interaction, charge-symmetry-breaking terms, four-nucleon forces, or other dynamical ingredients) must be added or modified so that the full set of low-energy n+3H observables is described consistently.
artifact.status_search_result: Searches indicate that the residual low-energy n+3H discrepancies, in particular for the spin-dependent / coherent scattering lengths, remain an unresolved feature of the four-nucleon problem. Standard local NN+3NF Hamiltonians such as AV18+UIX reproduce the triton binding energy but no single available interaction simultaneously fits all measured n+3H coherent and incoherent scattering lengths; nonlocal models (e.g. INOY) improve some observables but do not fully resolve the issue. Recent reviews and measurements continue to flag this as an open issue in the few-nucleon sector.

status_evidence.title: Universal correlations in pion-less EFT with the resonating group method: Three and four nucleons
status_evidence.snippet: Realistic NN potentials with exact few-body methods fail to reproduce three- and four-body binding energies, requiring 3N forces; tensions in four-nucleon observables remain.
status_evidence.claim: Four-nucleon low-energy observables remain a challenging open problem for realistic NN+3NF Hamiltonians.

status_evidence.title: Modern nuclear force predictions for the neutron-deuteron scattering lengths
status_evidence.snippet: Doublet nd scattering length is not reproduced by NN+3NF interactions without electromagnetic effects, indicating analogous tensions in low-energy few-nucleon scattering lengths.
status_evidence.claim: Analogous low-energy scattering-length discrepancies persist across realistic interactions.
